material_and_craftsmanship: Marked as I/I/II/II on the right and II/I/II/II on the left on Ìyẹ̀rosùn. Involves cooling shea butter (Òrí), Ewé Ègé, Ewé Arújẹ, and white pigeon sacrifice.
social_and_ritual_context: Divined when someone is surrounded by jealous peers or insidious slander. Commands calmness, discretion, and clean hands.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn ká ọwọ́ ìkà kúrò lórí awo; ẹni tó gbẹ́ kòtò kì í rí awo gbé ṣe. (Ìrosùn bound the hands of malice from the initiate; he who digs a pit finds no power to snare the righteous: Proclaiming victory over covert traps.)

Ìkà kò mọ̀ pé Ọlọ́run ń wo ilẹ̀; ìwà rere ni àbò tí kò lè wó. (The wicked plotter forgets that the Creator surveys the earth; righteous character is an indestructible fortress: Warning against deceit.)
A kì í fi ọwọ́ méjì gba ejò sí abíyá; awo tó fojú fò kì í jẹ oró. (One does not embrace a viper into one's bosom; an alert initiate never tastes bitter venom: Demanding strict boundary-setting.)

title: Ìrosùn Òtúúrúpọ̀n
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ìrosùn with the qualities of Òtúúrúpọ̀n.
description: Ìrosùn Òtúúrúpọ̀n is the #87 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ìrosùn on the right and Òtúúrúpọ̀n on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìrosùn (lifeblood, lineage memory) with Òtúúrúpọ̀n (carrying children upon the back, maternal care). Teaches that the continuity of human civilization rests upon nurturing vulnerable youth and honoring the labor of mothers.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìrosùn-Túúrúpọ̀n or Ìrosùn-Tọmọpọ̀n, celebrating infant pediatrics, safe deliveries, and maternal blood protection. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Favored by palace matrons supervising royal nurseries. Transatlantic Resilience: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Iroso Batrupon.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/I/II/II on the right and II/II/I/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Àbáwẹ̀, Ewé Ọ̀já-Ọmọ, cold maize gruel (Ẹ̀kọ), and snail broth.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for pediatric care, midwives, pregnant women, and civic leaders bearing collective community burdens. Protects young children.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn pọ̀n ọmọ mọ́ra, ó ti ẹnu-ọ̀nà àrùn; ọmọ lúwàbí kì í kú ní kékeré. (Ìrosùn strapped the infant to its back and locked the gate against illness; a child of destiny shall not perish in youth: Celebrating pediatric preservation.)

Ẹrù ọmọ kì í pa ìyá rẹ̀; ìfẹ́ inú la fi ń gbé iran tó ń bọ̀ ga. (The burden of an infant never breaks the mother's back; it is with devoted love that we elevate the generation to come: Praising maternal fortitude.)

A kì í fi ọmọdé dá ogun sílẹ̀; àwọn ọmọ wẹẹrẹ ni adé àlàáfíà ilé. (One does not endanger little children in community strife; young children are the crown of domestic peace: Mandating child protection.)

title: Ìrosùn Òtúá
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ìrosùn with the qualities of Òtúá.
description: Ìrosùn Òtúá is the #88 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ìrosùn on the right and Òtúá on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìrosùn (bloodline honor) with Òtúá (prayer, release, covenant). Teaches that freedom and peace arrive when ancestral grievances are released through sincere prayer and covenantal reconciliation.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìrosùn-Túá, governing the release of ancestral captives, spiritual covenant, and inter-religious tolerance. Imperial Era: Consulted when ratifying non-aggression treaties. Transatlantic Retention: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Iroso Tura.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as I/I/II/II on the right and I/II/I/I on the left. Involves Ewé Ẹfun, Ewé Tètè, white dove, honey, and white chalk (Ẹfun).
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during treaty ratifications, prisoner releases, and personal prayers for emancipation from spiritual bondage.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn tú àwọ̀n sílẹ̀, ó fi òmìnira wọ ìlú; ẹni tí ó ba gbé àlàáfíà ga kì í rí ogun. (Ìrosùn dismantled the snare and entered the city with freedom; he who exalts peace never faces warfare: Celebrating liberty and peace.)

Àdúrà tí a fi ọkàn mímọ́ gbà kì í ṣubú sílẹ̀; Ọlọ́run ń gbèjà olódodo. (The prayer offered with a pure conscience never falls flat; the Supreme Being defends the upright: Affirming divine deliverance.)

A kì í fi odi dí ọ̀nà àtiwọ ìmọ́lẹ̀; sùúrù la fi ń gbádùn àṣẹ àwọn àgbà. (One does not erect a wall to shut out the incoming light; it is with patience that one receives the blessings of the elders: Encouraging openness to truth.)

title: Ìrosùn Ìrẹtẹ̀
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ìrosùn with the qualities of Ìrẹtẹ̀.
description: Ìrosùn Ìrẹtẹ̀ is the #89 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ìrosùn on the right and Ìrẹtẹ̀ on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ìrosùn (lifeblood) and Ìrẹtẹ̀ (humility, earth, physical healing). Teaches that physical healing is achieved when human arrogance yields to therapeutic natural medicine and ecological balance.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìrosùn-Rẹtẹ̀ or Ìrosùn-Ate, governing the conquest of bone maladies, chronic infirmities, and humiliating skin conditions. Imperial Era: Consulted by priest-physicians during smallpox epidemics. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Cuban Ifá as Iroso Ate under Ọbalúayé.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/I/II/II on the right and I/I/II/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ìrẹtẹ̀, Ewé Gbégbé, roasted cornmeal, and palm wine for Ọbalúayé.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for patients suffering from dermatological ulcers, joint stiffness, or societal rejection. Demands strict hygiene and humility.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn rẹtẹ̀ mọ́lẹ̀, ó wo gbogbo àrùn sàn; àṣẹ Ọbalúayé kì í ṣe ohun àbùkù. (Ìrosùn bowed low to the earth and healed all diseases; the authority of Ọbalúayé is never an object of shame: Praising divine healing through humility.)

Ẹni tí ó tẹríba kì í tẹ́ nígbà ìpọ́njú; ìlera ni baba ọrọ̀. (He who bows his head never suffers humiliation during tribulation; vibrant health is the father of all wealth: Prioritizing health over vanity.)

A kì í fi ìgbéraga kọ ẹbọ ìwòsàn; ẹni tó fẹ́ gbádùn gbọ́dọ̀ gba ìmọ̀ràn àgbà. (One does not reject therapeutic sacrifice through arrogance; he who desires long life must heed elder counsel: Urging medical compliance.)

title: Ìrosùn Ọ̀ṣẹ́
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ìrosùn with the qualities of Ọ̀ṣẹ́.
description: Ìrosùn Ọ̀ṣẹ́ is the #90 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ìrosùn on the right and Ọ̀ṣẹ́ on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ìrosùn (bloodline honor, camwood) with Ọ̀ṣẹ́ (victory, sweetness, riverine joy). Demonstrates that lineage sorrows are sweetened and elevated when touched by Ọ̀ṣun's fertile blessing.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Abiodun, Rowland (2014). Yoruba Art and Language.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ìrosùn-Ṣẹ́, celebrating feminine grace, riverine wealth, and triumphant breakthrough from grief. Imperial Era: Consulted before royal festive banquets. Diaspora Survival: Maintained in Lucumí Ifá as Iroso She under Ọ̀ṣun.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as I/I/II/II on the right and I/II/I/II on the left. Involves Ewé Rinrin, Ewé Àjẹ́obàlé, river stones, brass bangles, and honey for Ọ̀ṣun.
social_and_ritual_context: Divined for seekers suffering long periods of sorrow, depression, or commercial failure. Restores marital and financial vitality.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn ṣẹ́gun ọ̀tá, ó fi oyin kún inú ilé; ayọ̀ ń bẹ fún ẹni tí ó ba nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí Ọ̀ṣun. (Ìrosùn vanquished the adversary and filled the house with honey; boundless joy awaits him who walks in covenant with Ọ̀ṣun: Celebrating fertile victory.)

Omi tútù kì í pọ́n lójú àgbàrá; ẹni tí ó ní sùúrù yóò jẹ adùn ayé. (Clear river water never turns muddy in the presence of seasonal flooding; he who possesses patience shall taste the sweetness of life: Preaching perseverance.)

Bí a bá ń wá ọlá, a gbọ́dọ̀ wẹ ọwọ́ mọ́; ìmọ́tótó ni baba àṣeyọrí. (If we seek majesty, we must wash our hands clean; immaculate purity is the foundation of triumph: Emphasizing clean ethics in wealth creation.)

title: Ìrosùn Òfún
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ìrosùn with the qualities of Òfún.
description: Ìrosùn Òfún is the #91 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ìrosùn on the right and Òfún on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ìrosùn (bloodline memory) and Òfún (divine white creation, Ọbàtálá). Encapsulates the complete transfiguration of generational curses into immaculate spiritual authority and peaceful longevity.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Idowu, E. Bolaji (1962). Olodumare: God in Yoruba Belief.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ìrosùn-Fún, the sacred chapter where ancestral camwood bloodlines are crowned in Ọbàtálá's pure white light. Imperial Era: Consulted during royal coronations. Diaspora Lineage: Preserved in Cuban Ifá as Iroso Fumbo.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/I/II/II on the right and II/I/II/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with pristine white pigeons, Ẹfun (chalk), Ewé Ọ̀bàtálá, and shea butter.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during deep identity crises, severe disputes, or ancestral crossroad determinations. Cleanses spiritual pollution and grants tranquil authority.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ìrosùn fún funfun gba adé Ọbàtálá, gbogbo ibi di ìmọ́lẹ̀; ikú kì í pa awo funfun. (Ìrosùn shone in immaculate white and received the crown of Ọbàtálá, transforming all darkness into radiance; death never claims the pristine initiate: Announcing spiritual transfiguration.)

Àlà funfun kì í dọ̀tí lójú Ọlọ́run; ẹni tí ó mọ́ ọkàn ni àpótí ọlá. (White linen never soils before the Creator; he who maintains a clean conscience is the treasury of majesty: Praising moral purity.)

Ẹni tí ó ru ẹbọ Òfún ti di odi mọ́ gbogbo ibi; a kì í fi ìméjì bọ Òrìṣà. (He who makes the sacrifice of Òfún has walled off all wickedness; one must not serve the divinities with double-mindedness: Demanding sincere devotion.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ogbè
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ogbè.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ogbè is the #92 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ogbè on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (whirlwind, sudden commerce, scarcity) on the right with Ogbè (cosmic radiance, expansion) on the left. Demonstrates that economic volatility and market fluctuations turn into monumental prosperity when guided by the radiant light of truth.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.
historical_timeline: Classical Ilé-Ifẹ̀ Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Sogbè or Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Ogbè, celebrated for transforming trade whirlwinds into boundless expansion and wealth. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Favored by caravans crossing imperial frontiers. Transatlantic Resilience: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Shobe.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and I on the left. Involves Ewé Ajé, Ewé Ṣaworo-pẹ́pẹ́, cowries, bananas, honey, and white rooster offerings.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during unpredictable commercial shifts or when launching major entrepreneurial ventures. Bestows commercial breakthrough.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín sogbè sọ owó di púpọ̀; oòrùn owúrọ̀ kì í pa olówó tì. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Sogbè multiplied wealth into abundance; the morning sun never fails the industrious laborer: Celebrating commercial triumph through diligence.)

Afẹ́fẹ́ kì í gbé ilé tí a fi òtítọ́ kọ́ lọ; awo tó mọ ìwà rẹ̀ kì í ṣubú. (The tempest never blows away a home founded upon truth; an initiate conscious of his character never falls: Affirming foundational stability.)

Bí a bá ń wá ajé, a kì í fi ẹ̀tàn gba owó lọ́wọ́ ará; ìwà rere ni baba ọrọ̀. (When seeking wealth, one does not swindle one's neighbor; righteous conduct is the true father of riches: Preaching commercial honesty.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀yẹ̀kú
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀yẹ̀kú is the #93 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ọ̀yẹ̀kú on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (whirlwind, instability) and Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (darkness, mortal transition). Teaches that the turbulent storms of physical existence are quelled through quiet ancestral contemplation and sacrificial propitiation.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Yẹ̀kú, governing the pacification of destructive tempests, averting sudden mortality, and clearing ancestral debts. Imperial Era: Consulted during outbreaks of drought or famine. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Yekun.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ọ̀dúndún, Ewé Tètè, black ram offering, and cool well water.
social_and_ritual_context: Divined during sudden community epidemics, family bereavement, or natural catastrophes. Quells panic and anchors communal peace.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín yẹ̀kú ti ẹnu-ọ̀nà ikú; afẹ́fẹ́ burúkú kì í fẹ́ wọ ilé awo. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀yẹ̀kú shut the portal of death; the malevolent gale never penetrates the home of the initiate: Proclaiming immunity from catastrophe.)

Ẹni tó bọ orí rẹ̀ ti la ewu kọjá; a kì í fi ẹ̀mí ṣeré nínú ìjì. (He who propitiates his own inner head has survived peril; one must never gamble with sacred life amidst the tempest: Prioritizing spiritual self-care.)

Bí òkùnkùn bá kù sẹ́yìn, ìmọ́lẹ̀ Ifá a yọ; sùúrù la fi ń rí àlàáfíà. (Though darkness lingers, the radiant light of Ifá shall appear; it is with patience that one receives enduring peace: Giving hope during grief.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìwòrì
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ìwòrì.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìwòrì is the #94 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ìwòrì on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (market vortex, trade) and Ìwòrì (spiritual sight, retrospection). Teaches that business volatility is mastered when foresight, historical analysis, and sharp vision guide economic choices.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fatunmbi, Awo Fa'lokun (1992). Iwa-Pele: Ifa Quest.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Wòrì, governing financial foresight, navigating fluctuating commodity markets, and avoiding contractual traps. Imperial Era: Consulted by merchants before entering interstate treaties. Diaspora Preservation: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Tanshela.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/I/I/II on the left. Involves Ewé Ajé, Ewé Pèrègún, cowries, and honey offerings.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast when entering significant financial partnerships or recovering from market panics. Demands sharp analytical auditing.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín wòrì wo iwájú ọjà, ó rí ajé; ojú tó ṣí sílẹ̀ kì í kùnà. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìwòrì surveyed the marketplace and seized prosperity; the open, vigilant eye never misses auspicious opportunities: Praising commercial foresight.)

A kì í fi owó ọjà bọ Òrìṣà láìní ìròyìn; ìṣirò pípé ni baba ọrọ̀. (One does not expend commercial capital upon ritual without accounting; rigorous bookkeeping is the father of wealth: Teaching fiscal discipline.)
Bí afẹ́fẹ́ bá ń fẹ́, awo gbọ́dọ̀ wo ibi tí eruku ń lọ; ìwòrì kì í kọsẹ̀. (When the wind blows, the initiate observes where the dust settles; true foresight never stumbles: Warning against blindness.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Òdí
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Òdí.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Òdí is the #95 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Òdí on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade windfall, whirlwind) with Òdí (rampart, container, seal). Teaches that rapid financial gains are useless unless contained within disciplined reserve systems and protected against waste.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Dí, governing the defensive containment of market earnings, boundary protection, and stopping leakages. Imperial Era: Consulted by royal treasurers to prevent embezzlement. Diaspora Lineage: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Bodi.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/II/II/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ètìpọ́nlà, Ewé Gbégbé, black soap, and sealed earthen vessels.
social_and_ritual_context: Divined when money disappears mysteriously, or when a business suffers from unexplained financial drain. Fortifies savings.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín dí àpò owó, ó ti ẹnu-ọ̀nà àbùkù; owó awo kì í sọnù sínú eruku. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín sealed the purse of wealth and shut the gate on shame; the initiate's earnings never vanish into dust: Celebrating financial containment.)

Odi tí a fi sùúrù mọ kì í jẹ́ kí ajé tú ká; awo tó mọ iṣẹ́ ṣe kì í ráhùn. (A wall constructed with patience never allows wealth to scatter; an industrious initiate never laments of poverty: Emphasizing disciplined savings.)

A kì í fi àpò tó ya kójọ owó; pẹ̀lẹ́pẹ̀lẹ́ la fi ń rán aṣọ ọlá. (One does not collect currency within a torn pouch; it is with gentle care that robes of majesty are stitched: Warning against careless waste.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìrosùn
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ìrosùn.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìrosùn is the #96 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ìrosùn on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade winds, scarcity) and Ìrosùn (camwood, bloodline honor). Demonstrates that ancestral heritage is sustained when commercial earnings are reinvested to honor family bloodlines.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Rosùn, governing lineage commerce, preserving ancestral estates, and avoiding spendthrift ruin. Imperial Era: Consulted when settling estate inheritances. Diaspora Survival: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Hermoso.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and I/I/II/II on the left. Involves Osùn, Ewé Ọ́kìkà, Ewé Ajé, honey, and guinea fowl sacrifice.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast when family estates are squandered by reckless heirs. Prescribes family council mediation and ancestral rededication.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín rosùn sọ owó di púpọ̀, ó fi ọlá bo ilé; afẹ́fẹ́ kì í gbé olóye lọ. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìrosùn multiplied wealth into abundance and clothed the home in majesty; the gale never carries away the wise thinker: Celebrating fiscal resilience.)

Owó kì í wọ ilé láì ní làálàá; awo tó gbọ́n kì í fi ọjọ́ ọrọ̀ gbàgbé ọjọ́ ebi. (Wealth never enters the home without honest labor; a wise initiate never forgets the days of famine during times of abundance: Preaching economic foresight.)

Bí ìjì bá ń jà, a kì í bọ́ sínú ọjà láìní ẹ̀ṣọ́; ìṣirò rere ni baba ajé. (When the storm rages, one does not venture to the market without protection; careful accounting is the father of wealth: Demanding fiscal discipline.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀bàrà
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ọ̀bàrà.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀bàrà is the #97 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ọ̀bàrà on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade vortex, wealth) with Ọ̀bàrà (manifestation, royal speech, kingship). Teaches that fair business diplomacy and honest speech convert mercantile profits into lasting royal prestige.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Bàrà, celebrated for eloquence in trade diplomacy, settling market strikes, and royal mercantile wealth. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Favored by the Ìyál'óde in trade negotiations. Diaspora Retention: Maintained in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Bara.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/II/II/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Àkòko, Ewé Ẹ̀lẹ́gẹdẹ, rooster, and white cowries.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for traders, guild leaders, and statesmen negotiating complex financial contracts. Inculcates fair dealing and eloquence.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín bàrà sọ ọ̀rọ̀ ọjà di oyin; ahọ́n rere ní ń fa ọlá mọ́ra. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀bàrà turned market speech into sweet honey; an eloquent, honest tongue is that which attracts majesty: Exalting diplomatic rhetoric.)
Ẹni tí ayé kẹ́gàn ní àná ló ń jẹ ọba lónìí; Ifá kì í fi olódodo sílẹ̀. (He whom the world mocked yesterday is crowned king today; Ifá never abandons the upright: Encouraging perseverance.)

A kì í fi irọ́ kọ́ ààfin ọlá; òtítọ́ inú nìkan ló lè gbé adé dúró lórí. (One does not erect the palace of majesty upon lies; only inner truthfulness can sustain the crown upon the head: Demanding ethical leadership.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀kànràn
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ọ̀kànràn.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀kànràn is the #98 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ọ̀kànràn on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade turbulence) and Ọ̀kànràn (thunder, moral conviction). Teaches that economic extortion must be courageously resisted; compromise with thieves destroys civic commerce.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Barnes, Sandra T. (1997). Africa's Ogun: Old World and New.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Kànràn, embodying lightning courage in commercial disputes, defending market rights, and repelling extortion. Imperial Era: Consulted during market guild revolts. Diaspora Lineage: Documented in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Pokon.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/II/II/I on the left. Involves Ẹdùn Àrá, Ewé Aragba, Ewé Ìná, and ram offerings for Ṣàngó.
social_and_ritual_context: Divined when merchants face extortion, racketeering, or violent seizure of property. Invokes Ṣàngó's protective justice.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín kànràn sọ òtítọ́ láì bẹ̀rù; àrá kì í pa ẹni tí kò hùwà ibi. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀kànràn proclaims the truth without fear; thunder never strikes down him who has committed no wickedness: Affirming divine defense.)

Bí a bá ń ja fún ẹ̀tọ́, a kì í fẹsẹ̀ fà sẹ́yìn; ọkàn líle la fi ń gbèjà ọjà. (When fighting for our rights, one does not retreat a step; stout-hearted courage is what defends the marketplace: Inspiring commercial justice.)

A kì í fi ìbínú gbin ẹ̀wọ̀n sí ilẹ̀; ìwà pẹ̀lẹ́ ni olórí gbogbo ogun. (One does not plant thorns of wrath in the soil; gentle self-control is the master of all conflict: Warning against hot-headedness.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ògúndá
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ògúndá.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ògúndá is the #99 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ògúndá on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (commerce, trade movement) and Ògúndá (iron, path-clearing). Demonstrates that trade routes flourish and commerce expands when backed by robust iron technology and secure roadways.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Gúndá or Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Dágò, governing transport technology, blacksmithing commerce, and clearing road blockades. Imperial Era: Consulted by caravan toll collectors and blacksmith guilds. Diaspora Preservation: Retained in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Dawan.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/I/I/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Pèrègún, Ewé Ọ́kìkà, forged iron nails, and roasted yam offerings.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for merchants embarking upon perilous long-distance trade or builders constructing commercial infrastructure.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ògún ti ọ̀nà ọjà pẹ̀lú irin, kò sí olè tó lè wọlé; àdá kì í wọ igbó lásán. (Ògún secured the trade route with forged iron, no thief can enter; the cutlass never enters the forest in vain: Celebrating trade security.)

Ẹni tí ó ń lu irin nínú àrọ kì í bẹ̀rù iná; iṣẹ́ ọwọ́ la fi ń di akọni. (He who hammers iron in the forge harbors no fear of sparks; it is through technical craft that heroes are made: Elevating metallurgical craftsmanship.)

A kì í fi irin dá ogun sí ara wa; àṣẹ Ògún wà fún àbò kì í ṣe fún ìparun. (One does not turn iron weapons upon one's own kin; Ògún's authority is given for protection, not senseless destruction: Demanding ethical tool usage.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀sá
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ọ̀sá.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀sá is the #100 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ọ̀sá on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade vortex) with Ọ̀sá (flight, sudden wind, astral spirits). Teaches that commercial wealth is vulnerable to sudden disasters; peace and fortune are safeguarded through respectful appeasement of the cosmic Mothers.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Lawal, Babatunde (1996). The Gelede Spectacle; Washington, Teresa N. (2005). Our Mothers, Our Powers, Our Texts.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Sá, governing protection against sudden financial collapse, market fires, and placating nocturnal astral societies. Imperial Era: Consulted when fires broke out in large urban markets. Diaspora Survival: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Boshe.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/I/I/I on the left. Involves Ewé Ọ̀jìjí, Ewé Òdúndún, eggs, honey, and white hen offerings to Ìyàmi.
social_and_ritual_context: Divined after commercial fires, sudden financial ruin, or severe nocturnal anxiety. Restores financial and emotional equilibrium.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín sá wọ àbò àwọn Ìyá, ó rí ìfọ̀kànbalẹ̀; ẹni tí àwọn àgbàlagbà bá gbè kì í sọnù. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín fled into the sanctuary of the Mothers and attained deep tranquility; he whom the elder matriarchs endorse never perishes: Commending spiritual sanctuary.)

Ẹyẹ kì í kọ odi tí a fi oyin kọ́; àlàáfíà ń bẹ fún ẹni tó bọ̀wọ̀ fún àwọn Ìyá. (The bird of the night never attacks a rampart consecrated with honey; peace reigns for him who honors the Mothers: Emphasizing gentle diplomacy with spiritual powers.)

Bí afẹ́fẹ́ bá ń jà, a kì í fi ilé sílẹ̀ láì ti ilẹ̀kùn; ìṣọ́ra ni odi awo. (When astral gales blow, one does not leave the dwelling unbarred; spiritual vigilance is the fortress of the initiate: Preaching preventive protection.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìká
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ìká.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìká is the #101 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ìká on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade, movement) with Ìká (restraint, coiling venom). Teaches that the poison of commercial fraud is disarmed through rigorous contractual transparency and refusal to participate in corrupt schemes.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Ká, governing the neutralizing of commercial fraud, contractual perjury, and stopping envious backbiters. Imperial Era: Consulted during market price-fixing disputes. Diaspora Lineage: Documented in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Bika.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and II/I/II/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ègé, Ewé Arújẹ, cooling shea butter, and white pigeon offerings.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast when a business person is targeted by envious competitors or malicious audits. Commands absolute transparency and serene restraint.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín ká ọwọ́ ìkà kúrò lórí awo; ẹni tó gbẹ́ kòtò kì í rí awo gbé ṣe. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín bound the hands of malice from the initiate; he who digs a pit finds no power to snare the righteous: Proclaiming victory over covert traps.)

Ìkà kò mọ̀ pé Ọlọ́run ń wo ilẹ̀; ìwà rere ni àbò tí kò lè wó. (The wicked plotter forgets that the Creator surveys the earth; righteous character is an indestructible fortress: Warning against deceit.)

A kì í fi ọwọ́ méjì gbá odi ẹjọ́ mú; sùúrù la fi ń tu àwọ̀n tí ó kọ́. (One does not dismantle an entangled dispute with violent fury; it is with patience that one untangles the knotted net: Recommending patient conflict resolution.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Òtúúrúpọ̀n
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Òtúúrúpọ̀n.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Òtúúrúpọ̀n is the #102 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Òtúúrúpọ̀n on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade provisions) and Òtúúrúpọ̀n (maternal care, carrying on the back). Teaches that during times of economic scarcity, communal solidarity and priority care for children guarantee civilizational survival.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Túúrúpọ̀n, governing family welfare, supporting expectant mothers, and managing domestic provisions during scarcity. Imperial Era: Consulted during food rationing in sieges. Diaspora Retention: Maintained in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Batrupon.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/II/I/II on the left. Involves Ewé Àbáwẹ̀, Ewé Ọ̀já-Ọmọ, cold maize gruel (Ẹ̀kọ), and snail broth.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for families managing scarce food supplies, pediatric clinics, and maternity wards. Strengthens domestic resilience.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín pọ̀n ọmọ mọ́ra, ó ti ẹnu-ọ̀nà àrùn; ọmọ lúwàbí kì í kú ní kékeré. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín strapped the infant to its back and locked the gate against illness; a child of destiny shall not perish in youth: Celebrating pediatric preservation.)

Ẹrù ọmọ kì í pa ìyá rẹ̀; ìfẹ́ inú la fi ń gbé iran tó ń bọ̀ ga. (The burden of an infant never breaks the mother's back; it is with devoted love that we elevate the generation to come: Praising maternal fortitude.)

A kì í fi ọmọdé dá ogun sílẹ̀; àwọn ọmọ wẹẹrẹ ni adé àlàáfíà ilé. (One does not endanger little children in community strife; young children are the crown of domestic peace: Mandating child protection.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Òtúá
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Òtúá.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Òtúá is the #103 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Òtúá on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade movement, whirlwind) with Òtúá (prayer, release, covenant). Teaches that prosperous commerce thrives only where peace covenants are upheld and bonded debts are mercifully restructured.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Túá, governing commercial treaties, release of bonded debtors, and peaceful trade pacts. Imperial Era: Consulted when lifting interstate trade embargoes. Transatlantic Survival: Preserved in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Alakentu.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/II/I/I on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Ẹfun, Ewé Tètè, white dove, honey, and white chalk (Ẹfun).
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during treaty ratifications, debt forgiveness arbitrations, and prayers for freedom from financial bondage.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín tú àwọ̀n sílẹ̀, ó fi òmìnira wọ ìlú; ẹni tí ó ba gbé àlàáfíà ga kì í rí ogun. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín dismantled the snare and entered the city with freedom; he who exalts peace never faces warfare: Celebrating liberty and peace.)

Àdúrà tí a fi ọkàn mímọ́ gbà kì í ṣubú sílẹ̀; Ọlọ́run ń gbèjà olódodo. (The prayer offered with a pure conscience never falls flat; the Supreme Being defends the upright: Affirming divine deliverance.)

A kì í fi odi dí ọ̀nà àtiwọ ìmọ́lẹ̀; sùúrù la fi ń gbádùn àṣẹ àwọn àgbà. (One does not erect a wall to shut out the incoming light; it is with patience that one receives the blessings of the elders: Encouraging openness to truth.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìrẹtẹ̀
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ìrẹtẹ̀.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ìrẹtẹ̀ is the #104 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ìrẹtẹ̀ on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Synthesis of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade instability) and Ìrẹtẹ̀ (humility, earth, convalescence). Teaches that economic and physical plagues are healed when human society practices radical humility, ecological stewardship, and sanitation.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Rẹtẹ̀, governing the conquest of economic contagions, bone maladies, and curing commercial disgrace. Imperial Era: Consulted during agrarian plagues. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Birete under Ọbalúayé.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and I/I/II/I on the left. Involves Ewé Ìrẹtẹ̀, Ewé Gbégbé, roasted cornmeal, and palm wine for Ọbalúayé.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for people suffering from sudden poverty, dermatological infections, or social ruin. Commands humility and strict environmental hygiene.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín rẹtẹ̀ mọ́lẹ̀, ó wo gbogbo àrùn sàn; àṣẹ Ọbalúayé kì í ṣe ohun àbùkù. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín bowed low to the earth and healed all diseases; the authority of Ọbalúayé is never an object of shame: Praising divine healing through humility.)

Ẹni tí ó tẹríba kì í tẹ́ nígbà ìpọ́njú; ìlera ni baba ọrọ̀. (He who bows his head never suffers humiliation during tribulation; vibrant health is the father of all wealth: Prioritizing health over vanity.)

A kì í fi ìgbéraga kọ ẹbọ ìwòsàn; ẹni tó fẹ́ gbádùn gbọ́dọ̀ gba ìmọ̀ràn àgbà. (One does not reject therapeutic sacrifice through arrogance; he who desires long life must heed elder counsel: Urging medical compliance.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀ṣẹ́
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Ọ̀ṣẹ́.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Ọ̀ṣẹ́ is the #105 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Ọ̀ṣẹ́ on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀wọ́nrín (trade movement, whirlwind) with Ọ̀ṣẹ́ (victory, sweetness, riverine joy). Teaches that the turbulent labor of commerce blossoms into overflowing joy and wealth when crowned with maternal sweetness and ethical beauty.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Abiodun, Rowland (2014). Yoruba Art and Language.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Ṣẹ́, celebrating the sweet victory of trade, riverine wealth, and banishing financial anxiety. Imperial Era: Consulted before royal markets opened in the capital. Diaspora Preservation: Documented in Cuban Ifá as Ojuani Boshe under Ọ̀ṣun.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/I/I on the right and I/II/I/II on the left on Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Rinrin, Ewé Àjẹ́obàlé, river stones, brass ornaments, and honey for Ọ̀ṣun.
social_and_ritual_context: Divined for merchants suffering from chronic trade depression or reproductive delay. Restores vibrant joy and commercial fertility.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín ṣẹ́gun ọ̀tá, ó fi oyin kún inú ilé; ayọ̀ ń bẹ fún ẹni tí ó ba nífẹ̀ẹ́ sí Ọ̀ṣun. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín vanquished the adversary and filled the house with honey; boundless joy awaits him who walks in covenant with Ọ̀ṣun: Celebrating fertile victory.)

Omi tútù kì í pọ́n lójú àgbàrá; ẹni tí ó ní sùúrù yóò jẹ adùn ayé. (Clear river water never turns muddy in the presence of seasonal flooding; he who possesses patience shall taste the sweetness of life: Preaching perseverance.)

Bí a bá ń wá ọlá, a gbọ́dọ̀ wẹ ọwọ́ mọ́; ìmọ́tótó ni baba àṣeyọrí. (If we seek majesty, we must wash our hands clean; immaculate purity is the foundation of triumph: Emphasizing clean ethics in wealth creation.)

title: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Òfún
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀wọ́nrín with the qualities of Òfún.
description: Ọ̀wọ́nrín Òfún is the #106 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the right and Òfún on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀wọ́nrín (whirlwind, commerce) and Òfún (divine white creation, Ọbàtálá). Encapsulates the complete transfiguration of earthly commercial struggles into immaculate spiritual authority, clean riches, and eternal peace.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Idowu, E. Bolaji (1962). Olodumare: God in Yoruba Belief.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀wọ́nrín-Fún, the sacred chapter where financial whirlwinds are sanctified in Ọbàtálá's pure white light. Imperial Era: Consulted during state coronations to secure agricultural abundance. Diaspora Survival: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Ojuani Bofun.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked on Ìyẹ̀rosùn as II/II/I/I on the right and II/I/II/I on the left. Involves pristine white pigeons, Ẹfun (chalk), Ewé Ọ̀bàtálá, and shea butter.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during profound identity crossroads, deep financial crises, or spiritual disorientation. Cleanses corrupt stains and grants serene majesty.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀wọ́nrín fún funfun gba adé Ọbàtálá, gbogbo ibi di ìmọ́lẹ̀; ikú kì í pa awo funfun. (Ọ̀wọ́nrín shone in immaculate white and received the crown of Ọbàtálá, transforming all darkness into radiance; death never claims the pristine initiate: Announcing spiritual transfiguration.)

Àlà funfun kì í dọ̀tí lójú Ọlọ́run; ẹni tí ó mọ́ ọkàn ni àpótí ọlá. (White linen never soils before the Creator; he who maintains a clean conscience is the treasury of majesty: Praising moral purity.)

Ẹni tí ó ru ẹbọ Òfún ti di odi mọ́ gbogbo ibi; a kì í fi ìméjì bọ Òrìṣà. (He who makes the sacrifice of Òfún has walled off all wickedness; one must not serve the divinities with double-mindedness: Demanding sincere devotion.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ogbè
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ogbè.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ogbè is the #107 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ogbè on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀bàrà (kingship, royal manifestation, eloquent speech) on the right with Ogbè (cosmic light, supreme authority, expansion) on the left. Encapsulates the ultimate philosophical thesis of Yorùbá royal statecraft: truthful speech endowed with divine light elevates the poorest seeker to the palace throne.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Abiodun, Rowland (2014). Yoruba Art and Language.
historical_timeline: Classical Ilé-Ifẹ̀ Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀bàrà-Bogbè or Ọ̀bàrà-Ogbè, celebrated throughout Yorùbá civilization as the supreme chapter of royal oratory, poetic mastery, and sudden elevation from poverty to kingship. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Consulted by the Aláàfin and Ọ̀yọ́ Mèsì when ratifying new dynastic appointments. Transatlantic Lineage: Universally revered in Cuban Santería/Ifá as Obara Bogbe.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed upon Ọpọ́n Ifá in two vertical columns: I/II/II/II on the right for Ọ̀bàrà and I on the left for Ogbè. Prepared with Ewé Àkòko, Ewé Ẹ̀lẹ́gẹdẹ (pumpkin leaves), rooster, white cowries, and honey.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for princes awaiting coronation, scholars delivering major orations, and entrepreneurs seeking epochal breakthroughs. Prescribes absolute honesty, clearing debts, and charity to the vulnerable.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà bogbè sọ òtítọ́, ó di ọba lórí àléfà; ahọ́n rere ní ń fa adé wá. (Ọ̀bàrà Bogbè spoke the unyielding truth and ascended the ancestral throne; an eloquent, honest tongue is that which attracts the crown: Exalting truth-telling in royal leadership.)

Ẹni tí ayé kẹ́gàn ní àná ló ń jẹ oyè ńlá lónìí; Ifá kì í fi ọmọ olódodo sílẹ̀ láìní ẹ̀ṣọ́. (He whom the world mocked yesterday is invested with supreme chieftaincy today; Ifá never leaves the child of the righteous without majestic adornment: Offering solace against persecution.)

A kì í fi irọ́ kọ́ ààfin ọlá; òtítọ́ inú nìkan ló lè gbé adé dúró lórí awo. (One does not build the palace of majesty with lies; only inner truthfulness can sustain the crown upon the initiate's head: Mandating inviolable integrity for leaders.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀yẹ̀kú
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀yẹ̀kú is the #108 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ọ̀yẹ̀kú on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (I/II/II/II: royal abundance, nobility, eloquence) on the right and Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (II/II/II/II: darkness, twilight, ancestral mortality) on the left of Ọpọ́n Ifá. Dialectically balances impending tragedy with divine economic redemption, teaching that the darkest hour of despair is the herald of sovereign breakthrough when sacrifice is performed.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination.
historical_timeline: Classical Ilé-Ifẹ̀ Antiquity (c. 9th–12th Century CE): Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Yẹ̀kú, governing the reversal of impending fatality and the sudden dawn of wealth following hardship. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́ Period (14th–18th Century CE): Consulted by the Aláàfin's council during periods of famine and regional siege to divine royal grain reserves. Transatlantic Retention: Preserved in Lucumí and Candomblé Ketu lineages as Obara Yeku, providing remedies against premature demise and financial ruin.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed upon Ọpọ́n Ifá with two columns: I/II/II/II on the right and II/II/II/II on the left. Involves cooling shea butter (Òrí), Ewé Òdúndún, Ewé Tètè, and a mature ram offering to Ṣàngó and the ancestors.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast when a prominent leader or merchant faces simultaneous sickness, financial debt, and public ridicule. Commands urgent purification to avert grief.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà yẹ̀ ikú fún olówó; òkùnkùn kì í pa iná tí Ọlọ́run bá tàn. (Ọ̀bàrà deflected death from the wealthy initiate; darkness never extinguishes the lantern lit by the Almighty: Proclaiming divine salvation from ruin.)

Bí ìyà bá ń jẹ awo, kò gbọdọ̀ sọ fún ọ̀tá; ọ̀la ń bọ̀ tí yóò kún fún ayọ̀. (When trial afflicts the initiate, he must not lament to adversaries; tomorrow arrives brimming with triumph: Exhorting dignified endurance.)
A kì í fi owó bọ̀rọ̀kọ̀ ra ikú; ìwà tútù ni àbò ẹ̀mí. (One does not purchase death with reckless wealth; gentle character is the true shield of longevity: Warning against arrogance in prosperity.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ìwòrì
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ìwòrì.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ìwòrì is the #109 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ìwòrì on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Combines Ọ̀bàrà (wealth, sovereignty) with Ìwòrì (deep spiritual insight, clairvoyance). Teaches that authentic royalty must cultivate inner spiritual vision, ensuring charisma is never hijacked by sycophants.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé: The Use of Plants in Yoruba Society.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Wòrì or Ọ̀bàrà-Kọ̀sọ̀, celebrating the fiery covenant between Ọ̀rúnmìlà and Ṣàngó. Imperial Era: Consulted before crowning princes of Ọ̀yọ́ to evaluate royal charisma. Diaspora Lineage: Maintained in Afro-Cuban Ocha-Ifá as Obara Koso, invoking thunderstone (Odù-Ará) protection.
material_and_craftsmanship: Marked as I/II/II/II on right and II/I/I/II on left of Ọpọ́n Ifá. Prepared with Ewé Iná, Ewé Rẹ̀rẹ̀, red rooster, and palm oil poured at the base of Ṣàngó's shrine.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during volatile leadership disputes, unmasking hypocrites within royal courts and securing immunity from witchcraft.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà Kọ̀sọ̀ kì í bẹ̀rù àrá; ọmọ Ṣàngó kì í kú sí ilé àjèjì. (Ọ̀bàrà Kọ̀sọ̀ fears no lightning; the child of Ṣàngó never perishes in a foreign land: Celebrating cosmic protection.)
Ojú tí ó rí awo kì í fọ́; òye inú ló ń tú àwọn ọ̀tá ká. (The eye that beholds the sacred mystery never goes blind; inner discernment scatters conspirators: Emphasizing spiritual insight.)
A kì í gbé iná sórí fìlà; ọ̀rọ̀ ọlọ́gbọ́n la fi ń pa iná ìbínú. (One does not carry burning embers upon the cap; the prudent word of the sage quenches furious wrath: Teaching peaceful statesmanship.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Òdí
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Òdí.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Òdí is the #110 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Òdí on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (wealth, expansion) and Òdí (protective wall, containment). Teaches that riches without institutional fortifications and moral discipline quickly evaporate.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Lawal, Babatunde (1996). The Gelede Spectacle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Dí, the protective fortress of prosperity, guarding harvests and childbirth. Imperial Era: Invoked by market guild leaders (Ìyál'ọ́jà) to safeguard marketplace revenues. Diaspora Preservation: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Obara Di.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and II/I/I/I on left on Ìyẹ̀rosùn. Uses Ewé Gbégbé, Ewé Rinrin, white pigeon, and cold cornstarch gruel (Ẹ̀kọ).
social_and_ritual_context: Cast when establishing new commercial enterprises or defending household estates from predatory rivals.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà dí odi yí ọrọ̀ ká; olè kì í wọ ilé tí awo fi òtítọ́ mọ. (Ọ̀bàrà erected a fortress around abundance; thieves cannot penetrate the compound built upon truth: Celebrating institutional security.)
Bí a bá lágbára láti kójọ, a gbọdọ̀ ní ọgbọ́n láti dáàbò bò ó. (If we possess the might to gather wealth, we must cultivate the wisdom to defend it: Extolling fiscal prudence.)

Ògiri tí kò l'áńfààní kì í jẹ́ kí alágẹmọ wọlé; ìwà tọ́ l'ó ń da odi sílẹ̀. (A wall without cracks denies admittance to the wall-gecko; upright character is an impregnable bastion: Teaching integrity.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ìrosùn
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ìrosùn.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ìrosùn is the #111 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ìrosùn on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (expansion) and Ìrosùn (ancestral bloodline, Osùn pigment). Teaches that the ancestral lineage must be washed clean of shame through honorable deeds and generous offerings.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀bàrà-Kosùn, celebrating royal bloodline vitality, ceremonial camwood ointment, and the cleansing of poverty. Imperial Era: Consulted during royal birth festivals. Transatlantic Retention: Revered in Afro-Cuban Ifá as Obara Koso/Obara Roso.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and I/I/II/II on left. Prepared with scarlet Osùn powder, Ewé Ètìpọ́nlà, rooster sacrifice, and consecrated palm wine.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast to break hereditary poverty, heal chronic circulatory ailments, and elevate a family's societal stature.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà pa osùn kùn orí ọlá; àbùkù àtijọ́ di ẹ̀yẹ lónìí. (Ọ̀bàrà rubbed sacred camwood upon the forehead of nobility; ancestral dishonor transforms into glory today: Proclaiming lineage redemption.)
Ẹ̀jẹ̀ rere l'ó ń gbé orí ga; a kì í fi ẹ̀gbin kọ́ ilé ọba. (Noble bloodline elevates the head; one never builds the king's palace upon filth: Affirming moral purity.)

Bí osùn bá wọ awọ, a máa fi àwọ̀ dídára hàn; bẹ́ẹ̀ ni orúkọ rere ń kàn sí gbogbo ayé. (When camwood penetrates the skin, it radiates lustrous beauty; so does a righteous name echo through all the world: Praising enduring reputation.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀wọ́nrín
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ọ̀wọ́nrín.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀wọ́nrín is the #112 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ọ̀wọ́nrín on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Pairs Ọ̀bàrà (wealth, sovereignty) with Ọ̀wọ́nrín (whirlwind, sudden reversal). Teaches that unexpected wealth requires humility and disciplined reinvestment lest the storm disperse it.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Wọ́nrín, governing sudden market windfalls and navigating capricious tides of fortune. Imperial Era: Consulted by caravan merchants before long-distance trade. Diaspora Retention: Maintained in Lucumí Ifá as Obara Juani.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and II/II/I/I on left. Involves Ewé Àjídèwe, Ewé Ọ̀bàrà, pigeon offering, and four cowrie shells deposited at a busy crossroads.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during sudden windfalls or rapid career transitions, prescribing moderation and charity to anchor good fortune.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Afẹ́fẹ́ Ọ̀bàrà wọ́nrín kó ọrọ̀ wọlé; ẹni tó bá ní sùúrù ni yóò jẹ ẹ́ pẹ́. (The whirlwind of Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀wọ́nrín swept wealth into the house; he who possesses patience shall enjoy it long: Exhorting fiscal discipline.)

Ọ̀rọ̀ tí a kò fojú rí kì í tú ilé olóye; ọlọ́gbọ́n ló ń ṣàkóso ìjì. (Unexpected fortune never dismantles the sage's household; the wise statesman tames the storm: Celebrating composure under windfall.)

A kì í fi owó ojijì ra ìbànújẹ́; ìrẹ̀lẹ̀ ni ìpìlẹ̀ ọrọ̀ tó ń tọ́jọ́. (One does not purchase sorrow with sudden windfall; humility is the foundation of enduring wealth: Condemning reckless ostentation.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀kànràn
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ọ̀kànràn.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀kànràn is the #113 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ọ̀kànràn on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (eloquence, majesty) and Ọ̀kànràn (uncompromising moral voice, thunderclap). Teaches that eloquence without moral truth is treacherous deception, while truthful speech yields everlasting honor.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Barnes, Sandra T. (1997). Africa's Ogun: Old World and New.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Kànràn, governing the court of conscience, integrity in commerce, and truthful speech. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Consulted by treasury auditors to evaluate tax collectors. Diaspora Tradition: Maintained in Cuba as Obara Kana.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and II/II/II/I on left. Prepared with Ewé Ọ́kìkà, Ewé Aragba, ram offering to Ṣàngó, and kola nuts.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast in civil disputes where perjury is suspected, commanding the parties to state the unvarnished truth under oath.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà sọ òtítọ́ kànràn lẹ́jọ́; ahọ́n tí kì í purọ́ kì í tọrọ jẹ. (Ọ̀bàrà spoke the resolute truth in judgment; the tongue that never lies never begs for sustenance: Affirming the sovereignty of honesty.)

Bí a bá ń wá ọlá, a kì í fi ẹ̀tàn gbé e ró; òtítọ́ inú ni ọ̀pá-ìtìlẹyìn ọba. (If we seek majesty, we do not erect it upon deceit; inner honesty is the king's firmest staff: Teaching ethical leadership.)

Ẹni tí ó ba purọ́ fún Ifá yóò rí ìdájọ́ Ṣàngó; àwọn Òrìṣà kórìíra ahọ́n méjì. (He who lies to the oracle shall confront the lightning judgment of Ṣàngó; the deities abhor double tongues: Demanding total transparency.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ògúndá
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ògúndá.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ògúndá is the #114 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ògúndá on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (wealth, nobility) and Ògúndá (iron, cutting force). Demonstrates that technological labor and blacksmith mastery transform raw ore into sovereign wealth and national defense.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Williams, Denis (1974). Icon and Image: A Study of Sacred Art in Five Continental Cultures.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀bàrà-Gúndá, the divine charter of blacksmith prosperity, mechanical invention, and surgical triumph. Imperial Era: Consulted by master smiths and armorers supplying cavalry blades. Diaspora Preservation: Preserved in Lucumí as Obara Ogunda.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and I/I/I/II on left. Prepared with Ewé Pèrègún, palm oil, roasted yam, iron slag from the forge, and a rooster to Ògún.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for blacksmiths, engineers, surgeons, and entrepreneurs embarking on heavy manufacturing ventures.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà la ọ̀nà irin, Ògún fi ọrọ̀ kúnlé; agbára ọwọ́ awo kì í di asán. (Ọ̀bàrà cleared the iron highway, and Ògún filled the storehouse with treasure; the skilled hand of the initiate never labours in vain: Extolling industrial industry.)

Irin tí a kò kàn kì í di idà ọlá; iṣẹ́ líle la fi ń kọ́ ọ̀làjú. (Iron that is never hammered never becomes a sword of glory; diligent industry is what constructs civilization: Praising productive labor.)

A kì í fi ojú àrùn wo ọmọ alágbẹ̀dẹ; iná àrò ni ń sọ irin di wúrà. (One does not pity the son of the blacksmith; the furnace flame is what refines crude iron into gold: Teaching resilience through adversity.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀sá
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ọ̀sá.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀sá is the #115 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ọ̀sá on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (majesty, riches) and Ọ̀sá (flight, nocturnal wind, spiritual storm). Teaches that the wealthy must honor the sacred feminine forces and the elderly to preserve their legacy from nocturnal fury.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Drewal, H.J. (1992). Gelede: Art and Female Power among the Yoruba.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Sá, governing diplomatic reconciliation with mystical nocturnal matriarchs (Ìyàmi Òṣòròngà). Imperial Era: Consulted by crown envoys to defuse palace revolts. Diaspora Tradition: Retained in Cuba as Obara Sa.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and II/I/I/I on left. Prepared with Ewé Ọ̀dúndún, Ewé Ajé, shea butter, eggs, and an offering plate placed at a junction for the Mothers.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during sudden household disturbances, nocturnal nightmares, or unexplained financial attrition, prescribing propitiation of the Mothers.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà sá kúrò nínú ìbínú, ó rí àlàáfíà gbà; ìbọ̀wọ̀ fún àwọn ìyá ló ń ti ẹnu ìbànújẹ́. (Ọ̀bàrà fled from wrath and embraced serene peace; reverence for the Mothers closes the jaws of sorrow: Teaching filial respect.)

Afẹ́fẹ́ kì í jà kí ó fọ́ ọpọ́n Ifá; ọlọ́gbọ́n kì í bẹ àwọn aláṣẹ níjà. (The gale never shatters the divination tray; the prudent diplomat never provokes sovereign custodians: Admonishing peaceable conduct.)

Bí a bá lágbára, a kì í fi ba ará ìlú lẹ́rù; ìwà tútù ló ń pa iná ẹ̀sùn. (Though we wield supremacy, we do not terrorize our compatriots; gentle character extinguishes the fire of accusations: Warning against tyranny.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ìká
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ìká.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ìká is the #116 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ìká on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (nobility, speech) and Ìká (wickedness, snare, bound cord). Teaches that integrity and divine vigilance dismantle the most insidious covert plots.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Epega, A.A. & Neimark, P. (1995). The Sacred Ifa Oracle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀bàrà-Ká, governing the unraveling of malicious conspiracies and unmasking deceitful associates. Imperial Era: Consulted during treason trials. Diaspora Preservation: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Obara Ka.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and II/I/II/II on left. Prepared with Ewé Arújẹ, Ewé Ègé, white dove, honey, and a severed cord symbolizing liberation.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast when an innocent person is framed by jealous business partners or family members.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà ká ọwọ́ ìkà kúrò lára ọmọ ọba; ẹni tó gbẹ́ kòtò sílẹ̀ yóò wọ̀ ọ́ fúnra rẹ̀. (Ọ̀bàrà plucked the hand of malice from the royal child; he who dug a pit shall plunge into it himself: Affirming poetic justice.)
A kì í fi ètàn mọ ilé ọlá; ọ̀pá òtítọ́ ni ń fó kòtò àdàkàdekè. (One does not build a house of honor upon intrigue; the staff of truth shatters the trap of duplicity: Extolling moral rectitude.)

Bí ọ̀tá bá kọ́ ọ̀wọ́, Ọlọ́run yóò fẹ́ wọn ká; awo olódodo kì í bẹ̀rù ẹ̀gún. (Though foes assemble in confederacy, the Almighty shall scatter them; the righteous initiate fears no hex: Proclaiming spiritual triumph.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Òtúúrúpọ̀n
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Òtúúrúpọ̀n.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Òtúúrúpọ̀n is the #117 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Òtúúrúpọ̀n on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (wealth) and Òtúúrúpọ̀n (carrying children upon the back). Teaches that the true measure of wealth is the health, education, and moral stature of the children who inherit it.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Túúrúpọ̀n, governing pediatric vitality, maternal blessings, and child continuity. Imperial Era: Favored by palace midwives and royal herbalists. Diaspora Lineage: Maintained in Lucumí as Obara Trupon.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and II/II/I/II on left. Prepared with Ewé Ọ̀já-Ọmọ, Ewé Àbáwẹ̀, snail broth, shea butter, and cold maize gruel (Ẹ̀kọ).
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for pregnant mothers, sick infants, and parents seeking generational blessings.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà pọ̀n ọmọ ọlá mọ́ra; ọmọ lúwàbí ni adé olówó. (Ọ̀bàrà strapped the noble infant to the back; virtuous children are the true crown of the wealthy: Celebrating generational lineage.)

Ẹrù ọmọ kì í wu ìyá lórí; pẹ̀lú ìfẹ́ la fi ń kọ́ ọmọdé ní ọ̀nà ìyè. (The burden of an infant never wearies the mother; it is with tender love that we guide the child along the path of life: Praising maternal devotion.)

Bí a bá ní ọrọ̀ tí a kò bímọ, ọrọ̀ di asán; ọmọ ni àkọsílẹ̀ tí kò lè parun. (If we amass wealth without offspring, riches become vanity; children are the living record that cannot perish: Articulating lineage continuity.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Òtúá
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Òtúá.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Òtúá is the #118 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Òtúá on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (wealth, sovereignty) and Òtúá (prayer, release, divine light). Teaches that wealth achieves cosmic sanction when dedicated to peace, philanthropy, and inter-community treaties.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Law, Robin (1977). The Oyo Empire c. 1600-c. 1836.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Túá, governing sacred covenants, divine intervention, and cross-cultural trade diplomacy. Imperial Era: Consulted when ratifying boundary accords with Dahomey and Nupe. Diaspora Tradition: Maintained in Cuba as Obara Tura.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and I/II/I/I on left. Involves Ewé Ẹfun, Ewé Tètè-Àgbalagba, honey, white dove, and white chalk (Ẹfun).
social_and_ritual_context: Cast during treaty ratifications, corporate mergers, and international diplomatic travels.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà tú àdúrà sílẹ̀, ọrọ̀ ń gbà wọlé; ẹni tí ó ba fẹ́ àlàáfíà kì í rí ogun. (Ọ̀bàrà poured forth sincere prayer, and abundance entered in; he who pursues peace never confronts warfare: Celebrating covenantal diplomacy.)

Àdúrà tí a fi ọkàn rere gbà ni Ọlọ́run ń kọ́kọ́ dáhùn; ìfẹ́ ará ilé ni ìmọ́lẹ̀ ayé. (The prayer offered with an upright heart is what the Creator answers first; fraternal love is the light of the cosmos: Teaching spiritual sincerity.)
A kì í fi ogun wá ọrọ̀; àdéhùn mímọ́ ló ń mú ìlú gbilẹ̀. (One does not seek wealth through reckless warfare; sacred covenants are what expand the commonwealth: Affirming peaceful commerce.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ìrẹtẹ̀
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ìrẹtẹ̀.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ìrẹtẹ̀ is the #119 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ìrẹtẹ̀ on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (dignity, wealth) and Ìrẹtẹ̀ (trampling illness, bodily purification). Teaches that royal dignity requires bodily sanctity and public hygiene; physical cleanliness mirrors moral purity.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Kẹtẹ̀ or Ọ̀bàrà-Rẹtẹ̀, governing dermatological healing, bodily purification, and victory over chronic pestilence. Imperial Era: Consulted during smallpox outbreaks. Diaspora Lineage: Maintained in Lucumí Ifá as Obara Rete.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and I/I/II/I on left. Prepared with Ewé Ìrẹtẹ̀, Ewé Ṣaworo, sulfur-and-chalk bath, and cold shea butter ointment.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for chronic ailments, bodily sores, or spiritual uncleanness, commanding herbal baths and dietary taboos.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà tẹ àrùn mọ́lẹ̀, ó fi ara dídára wọlé; àlàáfíà ara ni gbongbo gbogbo ọrọ̀. (Ọ̀bàrà trampled illness underfoot and entered with radiant health; sound physical vitality is the root of all wealth: Praising holistic wellness.)

Bí ara kò bá le, ọrọ̀ kò lè dùn; ìmọ́tótó ni aṣọ àwọn olóye. (If the physical body lacks vigor, wealth loses its sweetness; cleanliness is the vestment of the wise: Teaching public health and hygiene.)

A kì í fi ẹ̀gbin kùn orí àṣẹ; ẹni tó mọ́ lójú àwọn Òrìṣà kì í dọ̀tí. (One does not anoint the brow of authority with defilement; he who is clean in the sight of the deities never suffers corruption: Affirming sacred purity.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀ṣẹ́
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Ọ̀ṣẹ́.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Ọ̀ṣẹ́ is the #120 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Ọ̀ṣẹ́ on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (wealth, sovereignty) and Ọ̀ṣẹ́ (sweetness, beauty, victory through joy). Teaches that harsh force repels fortune, whereas gracious beauty, honeyed speech, and artistic sweetness conquer all opposition.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Badejo, Diedre L. (1996). Ọ̀ṣun Ṣèègèsí: The Elegant Deity of Wealth, Power, and Femininity.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Ṣẹ́, the conduit of Ọ̀ṣun's riverine fortune, auditory honey, and artistic brilliance. Imperial Era: Consulted by court bards, royal jewelers, and musicians. Diaspora Tradition: Celebrated in Afro-Cuban Ocha-Ifá as Obara She.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and I/II/I/II on left. Prepared with Ewé Ọ̀ṣun, pure wild honey, bronze bell (Aago), yellow cloth, and river pebbles.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for artists, musicians, traders, and women seeking matrimonial sweetness and financial breakthrough.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà bu oyin sí ahọ́n, ó fi adùn gba ilé ọba; ọ̀rọ̀ dídùn ni ń yọ ejò nínú ihò. (Ọ̀bàrà poured honey upon the tongue and claimed the palace with sweetness; pleasant speech is what coaxes the serpent from its hole: Praising the power of gracious diplomacy.)

Odò Ọ̀ṣun kì í gbẹ kí ẹja má rí ibi lúwẹ̀ẹ́; ore-ọ̀fẹ́ Ọlọ́run kì í kùnà. (The river of Ọ̀ṣun never dries up so that the fish lack room to swim; the benevolent grace of the Almighty never falters: Affirming boundless abundance.)
A kì í fi ibi san ore; ẹni tó bá fi oyin kẹ́ ayé yóò rí adùn jẹ. (One does not repay kindness with evil; he who sweetens the world with honey shall savor eternal joy: Teaching moral reciprocity.)

title: Ọ̀bàrà Òfún
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀bàrà with the qualities of Òfún.
description: Ọ̀bàrà Òfún is the #121 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀bàrà on the right and Òfún on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀bàrà (wealth, nobility) and Òfún (white chalk, primal purity, senior creation). Teaches that the ultimate summit of prosperity is stainless moral character (Ìwà-tútù) and reverence for the aged.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Lawal, Babatunde (1996). The Gelede Spectacle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀bàrà-Fún, the apex chapter of the Ọ̀bàrà cycle, governing Obàtálá's white cloth covenant and elder wisdom. Imperial Ọ̀yọ́: Consulted when selecting the most senior noble elders. Diaspora Lineage: Maintained in Lucumí Ifá as Obara Fun.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as I/II/II/II on right and II/I/II/I on left. Involves pure white cloth (Aṣọ Funfun), white chalk (Ẹfun), shea butter, cold spring water, and a white pigeon to Obàtálá.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast for high chieftains, elder statesmen, and community leaders seeking divine longevity and spotless moral reputation.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀bàrà wọ aṣọ funfun, ó fi ìwà tútù gba orí ayé; a kì í fi ẹ̀gbin kùn aṣọ Obàtálá. (Ọ̀bàrà donned the spotless white robe and conquered the world through gentle character; one never soils the sacred vestment of Obàtálá: Reverencing stainless moral integrity.)

Ọlá tí kò ní ẹ̀tàn ló ń di funfun réfeté; orúkọ rere kọjá wúrà àti fàdákà. (Nobility devoid of guile shines with brilliant whiteness; a good name is far more precious than gold and silver: Affirming transcendent virtue.)
Àgbà tí ó ní sùúrù ló ń jẹ adé ọlá; ìrẹ̀lẹ̀ ni ìyá gbogbo ìwà rere. (The elder who masters patience inherits the crown of majesty; humility is the mother of all virtues: Celebrating elder wisdom.)

title: Ọ̀kànràn Ogbè
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀kànràn with the qualities of Ogbè.
description: Ọ̀kànràn Ogbè is the #122 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀kànràn on the right and Ogbè on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀kànràn (II/II/II/I: moral conscience, thunder voice) on right and Ogbè (I/I/I/I: pristine light, opening road) on left. Dialectically represents righteous indignation illumined by cosmic light, declaring that when truth speaks without fear, all paths open.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Barnes, Sandra T. (1997). Africa's Ogun: Old World and New.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀kànràn-Sodé or Ọ̀kànràn-Ogbè, announcing the sudden dawn of truth, judicial vindication, and the banishment of conspirators. Imperial Era: Consulted before judicial trials at Akẹ̀sán market. Diaspora Preservation: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Okanran Sode.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed on Ọpọ́n Ifá as II/II/II/I on right and I/I/I/I on left. Prepared with Ewé Tètè, Ewé Gbégbé, rooster to Ṣàngó, and four fresh kola nuts.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast when someone is wrongly indicted or trapped in bureaucratic deception, releasing immediate legal breakthrough.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀kànràn sọ̀rọ̀ sí gbangba, Ogbè la ojú ọ̀nà; òtítọ́ inú kì í ṣubú sílẹ̀. (Ọ̀kànràn proclaimed truth in the public square, and Ogbè opened the highway; inner righteousness never collapses: Celebrating courage and transparency.)
Bí ilẹ̀ bá mọ́, olè a gbọ́n; ìmọ́lẹ̀ òtítọ́ ló ń lé òkùnkùn ẹ̀tàn sá. (When dawn breaks, the thief scatters; the light of truth chases away the darkness of deception: Exalting triumphant clarity.)

A kì í fi ẹ̀rù bo ojú ọ̀rọ̀; ahọ́n tí kì í purọ́ ní ń gba aṣẹ lọ́wọ́ ọba. (One does not conceal the truth beneath cowardice; the tongue that never lies receives authority from the king: Inspiring fearless integrity.)

title: Ọ̀kànràn Ọ̀yẹ̀kú
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀kànràn with the qualities of Ọ̀yẹ̀kú.
description: Ọ̀kànràn Ọ̀yẹ̀kú is the #123 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀kànràn on the right and Ọ̀yẹ̀kú on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀kànràn (fire, thunder) and Ọ̀yẹ̀kú (darkness, mortality). Teaches that the fiery wrath of justice must be tempered with solemn ancestral pacification to avoid mutual destruction.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Verger, Pierre (1995). Ewé.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Known as Ọ̀kànràn-Yẹ̀kú, governing the aversion of sudden accidental deaths, warding off lightning strikes, and pacifying ancestral guardians. Imperial Era: Consulted during terrifying thunderstorms. Diaspora Lineage: Retained in Lucumí as Okanran Yeku.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/II/I on right and II/II/II/II on left. Involves Ewé Òdúndún, Ewé Rinrin, black cloth, he-goat, and cold water poured over thunderstones.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast to neutralize ominous portents, pacify Ṣàngó's anger, and protect households from fiery accidents.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀kànràn yẹ̀ ikú lórí awo; àrá kì í pa ẹni tí ó tẹríba fún àwọn àgbà. (Ọ̀kànràn averted death from the initiate's head; thunder never strikes down him who bows before the elders: Affirming filial reverence and protection.)
Ẹni tí ó ba gbọ́ ikilọ̀ kì í bá ogun kọjú; ìṣọ́ra ni bàbá àlàáfíà. (He who heeds sacred warnings never collides with catastrophe; vigilant foresight is the father of peace: Teaching prudent caution.)
A kì í fi iná kọ́ ilé koríko; ọ̀rọ̀ sùúrù ló ń paná ìjà. (One does not build a thatch cottage with burning flames; peaceful speech quenches the fire of conflict: Condemning reckless belligerence.)

title: Ọ̀kànràn Ìwòrì
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀kànràn with the qualities of Ìwòrì.
description: Ọ̀kànràn Ìwòrì is the #124 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀kànràn on the right and Ìwòrì on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀kànràn (voice of judgment) and Ìwòrì (deep spiritual sight). Teaches that righteous judgment must always be guided by thorough forensic investigation and deep spiritual discernment.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Drewal, H.J. & Pemberton, J. (1989). Yoruba.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀kànràn-Wòrì or Ọ̀kànràn-Adigun, governing profound diagnostic clairvoyance, unmasking charlatans, and piercing deceptive façades. Imperial Era: Consulted by military scouts. Diaspora Tradition: Maintained in Cuba as Okanran Giwori.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/II/I on right and II/I/I/II on left. Prepared with Ewé Ìyàyà, Ewé Iná, ram offering, and clear river water used to wash the initiate's eyes.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast when navigating complex interpersonal deception or forensic legal investigations.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀kànràn wò inú ọ̀rọ̀, ó rí gbongbo ètàn; ojú awo kì í fò lórí òtítọ́. (Ọ̀kànràn gazed into the core of the matter and identified the root of deceit; the eye of the initiate never overlooks the truth: Praising investigative acumen.)

A kì í fọwọ́ kọ́ ìbọn kí a má le ta á; ẹni tó mọ ìtàn kì í dáràn. (One does not prime the musket without knowing how to aim; he who knows the roots of history never stumbles into catastrophe: Teaching historical mastery.)

Àìwòkíyèsí ni ń mú awo ṣe àṣìṣe; ojú tútù ló ń rí ohun tí ń bẹ nínú ihò. (Inattentiveness is what causes the initiate to blunder; calm eyes perceive that which hides deep inside the cavern: Warning against haste in judgment.)

title: Ọ̀kànràn Òdí
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀kànràn with the qualities of Òdí.
description: Ọ̀kànràn Òdí is the #125 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀kànràn on the right and Òdí on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀kànràn (defensive vigilance) and Òdí (fortress wall). Teaches that the moral courage of a community is its most impenetrable rampart against external invasion.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1976). Ifá: An Exposition of Ifá Literary Corpus; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Lawal, Babatunde (1996). The Gelede Spectacle.
historical_timeline: Classical Antiquity: Codified as Ọ̀kànràn-Dí, governing the protective barrier around the domestic sanctuary, immune defense, and maternal care. Imperial Era: Consulted before fortifying city gates. Diaspora Preservation: Preserved in Lucumí Ifá as Okanran Di.
material_and_craftsmanship: Inscribed as II/II/II/I on right and II/I/I/I on left. Prepared with Ewé Gbégbé, fresh palm fronds (Mọ̀rìwò), iron nails, and rooster offering deposited at compound threshold.
social_and_ritual_context: Cast to protect families against midnight intruders, jealous neighbors, and spiritual witchcraft.
proverbs_and_oral_traditions: Ọ̀kànràn dí ẹnu-ọ̀nà fún ibi; odi tí Ifá mọ kì í wó láé. (Ọ̀kànràn sealed the portal against malevolence; the fortress that Ifá constructs never collapses: Proclaiming impenetrable security.)

Bí ilé bá l'álàáfíà, ìta kò lè mú un; ìfọwọ́sowọ́pọ̀ ni àbò ìdílé. (If the household possesses concord, outside hostility cannot prevail; mutual cooperation is the shield of the lineage: Teaching family unity.)

A kì í fi ọ̀bẹ gé ọwọ́ ara ẹni; aládùúgbò rere kọjá ará ilé tí kò sí níbẹ̀. (One does not use the blade to sever one's own hand; a harmonious neighbor is more valuable than an absent kinsman: Praising community solidarity.)

title: Ọ̀kànràn Ìrosùn
cosmological_meaning: Harmonizes the principles of Ọ̀kànràn with the qualities of Ìrosùn.
description: Ọ̀kànràn Ìrosùn is the #126 chapter of the 256 Odù Ifá, formed by combining Ọ̀kànràn on the right and Ìrosùn on the left of the Ọpọ́n Ifá.
etymology_and_philosophy: Conjunction of Ọ̀kànràn (voice of justice) and Ìrosùn (bloodline, ancestral camwood). Teaches that true familial honor requires forgiving ancient grievances and uniting under righteous truth.
provenance_and_citations: Abímbọ́lá, Wándé (1975). Sixteen Great Poems of Ifá; Bascom, William (1969). Ifa Divination; Fadipe, N.A. (1970). The Sociology of the Yoruba.
